Investment banking fees surged, equity underwriting was up 77% year-over-year, and management raised full-year NII and ROTCE guidance — all pointing to positive momentum heading into year-end.

company_items.summary: Citigroup posted Q3 EPS of $2.85, up 27% year-over-year and ahead of the Street estimate of $2.65. Revenue came in at $23.85 billion versus the $23.72 billion estimate, with expense discipline pushing the efficiency ratio to 59% versus the expected 60.7%. The company raised full-year NII guidance to mid-to-high 6% growth (from 5-6%) and lifted ROTCE guidance to 11% (from 10-11%), while equity underwriting surged 77% year-over-year.

sectors: Large-cap bank earnings showing strength in investment banking, with FICC up 4%, IB fees up 9%, and equity underwriting surging 77% year-over-year at Citigroup — a positive read-through for the broader financials sector heading into the rest of earnings season.
tts_summary: Here's your final earnings recap of the morning, and it's a clean one. Citigroup just reported third quarter results and it's a solid beat across the board. EPS came in at two dollars and eighty-five cents, up 27% year-over-year, well ahead of the Street's two-sixty-five estimate. Revenue was twenty-three point eight five billion versus the twenty-three point seven two billion consensus — a modest beat on the top line, but the real story is what happened below it. The efficiency ratio improved 290 basis points to 59%, beating expectations of 60.7%, meaning Citi is doing a better job controlling costs. Provisions were also lighter than feared at two point five eight billion versus the two point six five billion estimate, and they only built three hundred sixty-nine million in reserves during the quarter, which tells you management isn't bracing for a credit cliff. Inside the investment bank, fixed income currency and commodities revenue rose 4% to four point three eight billion, edging past the four point two six billion estimate. Equities was the one soft spot — one point seven two billion versus the one point seven seven billion estimate, so a slight miss there. But IB fees were strong, up 9% to one point three five billion versus one point two six billion expected, and equity underwriting absolutely ripped — up 77% year-over-year. That's a significant number. On guidance, management tweaked the full-year outlook higher. They now see net interest income growing in the mid-to-high 6% range, up from the prior 5 to 6% guide. Return on tangible common equity is now seen at 11%, up from the prior 10 to 11% range. The directional read here is clearly positive for Citigroup and likely supportive for the broader financials sector as earnings season rolls on. Watch for read-throughs to other large-cap banks — strong underwriting and fee activity at Citi bodes well for peers yet to report.
